scenarios.title: Create a project from a starter
scenarios.coverage: none yet — project creation is built (`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/Onboarding.tsx`), the STARTER it describes is not: nothing offers a template to create from
scenarios.expected_result: one persistent Project exists independently of any goal; saved setup and managed activation are distinct, and only managed activation promises an admitted PM.
scenarios.errors_recovery: missing input or scope shows an inline error and preserves the draft; admission/binding failure blocks activation and links to the failed gate; save failure retains the entire draft for retry.

scenarios.title: Create a portfolio observer
scenarios.coverage: none yet — an observer that watches across projects needs a producer other than the operator (M20), which is unscheduled
scenarios.expected_result: an ordinary Project targets all current/future projects and has no implied write authority over them.
scenarios.errors_recovery: dynamic scope without operator confirmation remains blocked; an effect-level connection binding is rejected unless a specific grant exists.

scenarios.title: Add or replace an admitted agent
scenarios.expected_result: the project gains the agent capability; existing runs remain pinned and routines retain their identities and schedules.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a grant above project ceiling is blocked; revision conflict shows the newer diff and asks the operator to reapply the draft.

scenarios.title: Provider cannot be bound
scenarios.expected_result: no project access is created and no discovered provider is presented as compatible merely because it exists.
scenarios.errors_recovery: registry unavailable is separate from admission failure; retry registry or complete the named Fabric compatibility gate.

scenarios.title: Connect and scope an external account
scenarios.expected_result: one estate connection is reused through a narrower versioned project binding and secret values never enter project configuration.
scenarios.errors_recovery: OAuth expiry offers retry; no selected resource/agent blocks save; removed resource marks only that binding stale and offers reselection.

scenarios.title: Scan all project cards
scenarios.expected_result: the operator can identify which project and dimension needs attention without accepting an unsupported composite status.
scenarios.errors_recovery: projector failure keeps last data as stale with retry; one source failure affects only its dimension.

scenarios.title: Open an affected project from attention
scenarios.expected_result: the source of attention is traceable from estate card to project and exact run/observation.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a missing receipt is displayed as unverified with refresh/trace recovery, never replaced by an agent conclusion.

scenarios.title: Inspect and recover a run
scenarios.expected_result: the operator understands what became true and performs at most one authorised recovery action.
scenarios.errors_recovery: reconnect resumes from monotonic event id; unauthorised action preserves the run and opens approval; retry exhaustion returns best partial result.

scenarios.title: Replace an agent without moving its routine
scenarios.expected_result: schedule and history survive provider replacement; only future runs use the successor binding.
scenarios.errors_recovery: no eligible replacement leaves the routine waiting/disabled with a named reason; active run is never rebound.

scenarios.title: Observer submits a proposal
scenarios.expected_result: evidence crosses the project boundary as a proposal, not a direct graph or memory write.
scenarios.errors_recovery: target missing/retired or PM unavailable leaves the finding unresolved with a recoverable routing error.

scenarios.title: Target PM resolves a proposal once
scenarios.coverage: the resolve-once half only — `apps/desktop/src/main/commands/proposalCommands.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/proposals.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/launch/ObligationActs.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/launch/BoardScreen.test.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/proposals.test.ts`. NOT covered: SCR-11, the resolution preview of step 2, `supersede`, and the cross-project links of step 3.
scenarios.expected_result: target project retains decomposition authority and the same proposal cannot produce duplicate work.
scenarios.errors_recovery: already-resolved proposal shows the existing resolution and disables duplicate action; stale evidence blocks resolution until refreshed.

scenarios.title: Promote memory through an accepted artifact
scenarios.expected_result: no project writes another project's memory directly and every promoted fact retains provenance.
scenarios.errors_recovery: missing evidence/confidence blocks promotion; contradictory estate knowledge requires explicit supersession rather than overwrite.

scenarios.title: Join an estate with explicit roles
scenarios.expected_result: the person joins with informed, attributable scope and receives no credential or implicit access outside the declared roles.
scenarios.errors_recovery: expired or changed invitation offers refresh/contact-owner; partial acceptance is not silently inferred.

scenarios.title: Resolve an interaction from a role workspace
scenarios.expected_result: one human contribution closes or advances the interaction without duplicate effects or unrelated estate exposure.
scenarios.errors_recovery: already-resolved item opens the existing receipt; denied effect preserves the draft and requests a grant; stale evidence requests refresh.

scenarios.title: Adapt an existing repository into a provider
scenarios.expected_result: the existing project remains architecturally owned by its author and produces a reproducible provider bundle or a precise failed gate.
scenarios.errors_recovery: integrity mismatch or unreviewed change plan stops before writes; local failure preserves report and offers a regenerated fix recipe.

scenarios.title: Create and admit a new provider
scenarios.expected_result: exact provider revision is admitted; no project access exists until the separate binding is saved; canary/promotion history remains attached to the revision/binding.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a passing local report cannot override failed independent conformance; binding ceiling/budget failures preserve admission and return to setup.

scenarios.title: Bootstrap or conformance fails safely
scenarios.expected_result: no admission, binding, credential or partial hidden installation exists; recovery preserves user code and evidence.
scenarios.errors_recovery: cleanup failure lists remaining generated paths without deleting user-owned files; expired short-lived exchange can be reissued without changing the recipe target.

scenarios.title: Add a provider view to a role workspace
scenarios.expected_result: the role gains a useful interface while PassionCode.ai retains layout, permission, accessibility and action authority.
scenarios.errors_recovery: missing fallback, overbroad scope, overlap, invalid span, focus-order failure or unadmitted revision blocks publish, identifies the tile and offers the nearest valid placement/order.

scenarios.title: Resolve a customer request with human fallback
scenarios.expected_result: the customer receives one attributable response; unresolved or sensitive work has one human owner; product work crosses as a proposal rather than a direct backlog mutation.
scenarios.errors_recovery: identity ambiguity requests human selection without merging customers; missing knowledge blocks confident answer; expired grant preserves response draft.

scenarios.title: Turn a production signal into a verified release
scenarios.expected_result: source signal, accepted work, code/test evidence, authorization, release receipt and recovery observation form one trace.
scenarios.errors_recovery: checker rejection returns to its producer without advancing; unavailable policy fails closed at release; monitor timeout leaves incident unresolved.

scenarios.title: Research, validate, publish and measure content
scenarios.expected_result: every public artifact is sourced, independently checked, authorized, receipted and connected to its measured feedback.
scenarios.errors_recovery: no channel identity or expired grant blocks publication but preserves approved draft; API failure reconciles before retry to prevent duplicate posts.

scenarios.title: Create and connect scoped MCP access
scenarios.expected_result: the external client is connected through one immutable, expiring Project-scoped binding and no owner session or downstream credential was shared.
scenarios.errors_recovery: missing scope/expiry blocks issuance; failed discovery identifies transport/auth/version/scope layer; a lost one-time value is rotated, never recovered.

scenarios.title: External agent participates within its MCP scope
scenarios.expected_result: the external agent participates through the same Project, policy, journal, checker and durable WorkflowRun lifecycle as an internal request.
scenarios.errors_recovery: dropped connection resumes by Task/Run id; conflicting idempotency reuse is rejected; failed/cancelled Run preserves partial evidence and current state.

scenarios.title: MCP access is denied or revoked safely
scenarios.expected_result: excluded or revoked access produces no unauthorized read/mutation, while existing Run state remains truthful and separately controllable.
scenarios.errors_recovery: failed revocation leaves old status visible and offers retry; cancellation request reports cooperative/current state rather than “cancelled” until proven.

scenarios.title: Work in a project's hosted terminal
scenarios.expected_result: the session is the one the agent actually runs in, typeable and reattachable, and its lifecycle exists as journal events with receipts. It lives in its own window so the project panel stays readable behind it.
scenarios.errors_recovery: spawn failure names the cwd and binary checked and offers retry without journalling an open; a killed PTY marks the tab ended, never silently blank.

scenarios.title: Follow the estate through the journal feed
scenarios.coverage: step 3 and its fallback — `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/Feed.test.tsx`; every registered event type has a sentence, both directions — `scripts/check-design.mjs`. Replay, ordering and reconnection (steps 1, 2, 5): none yet
scenarios.expected_result: the feed is a view over the durable trace (ADR-0027); every fact opens its receipt, and every row is legible to the person being asked to check it. A receipt nobody can read is not a receipt.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a Realtime outage degrades to on-demand replay with a stale banner; the feed never invents order — it shows the table's. An event with no sentence falls back to the RAW TYPE and never to the lookup key: a missing key renders as itself, and `event.task.moved@1` on screen is the identifier plus a prefix that means nothing.

scenarios.title: Approve, refuse or watch the floor refuse
scenarios.expected_result: escalation is the exception and every resolution carries a receipt; nothing floored happens silently and nothing floored defaults open.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a resolution that fails to persist retries without double-resuming the node (idempotent by question id); policy `indeterminate` is shown as a denial with diagnostics, never as pending.

scenarios.title: Open a project as a tab and configure it
scenarios.expected_result: projects are browser-like tabs over persistent workspaces; every configuration change is an event with a revision, not a silent mutation.
scenarios.errors_recovery: an empty name blocks the save with the draft preserved; a failed append surfaces the error banner and leaves the header unchanged.

scenarios.title: Launch an agent and open its session window
scenarios.expected_result: agents are sessions with a visible short status on the project page and a full terminal in their own window; closing a window is not ending work.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a spawn failure names the program and directory and journals nothing as opened; an ended session remains as a dismissible tile with its exit code.

scenarios.title: Read the project workspace canvas
scenarios.expected_result: the workspace exists as a slot layout the operator can read today and providers can render into later, without the layout moving when they do.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a widget whose projection is unavailable states that its evidence is stale instead of rendering zero as a fact.

scenarios.title: Onboard a project in a new tab
scenarios.expected_result: onboarding is an addressable draft; an unsaved draft creates no business Project. A saved Project exposes its purpose and explicit setup state, including deferred PM/executor. Native store/IPC evidence remains separate from target prototype behavior.
scenarios.errors_recovery: an empty name blocks the save with the draft preserved; a failed append leaves the draft editable and shows the error. Late hydration merges saved drafts with current typing without switching away from the new draft; no save runs before hydration. An unreadable file is not replaced by defaults or new typing, and the read problem remains visible beside any dropped-tab notice.

scenarios.title: Ask for work and watch what it opened
scenarios.expected_result: asking for work is one field and one button; what was asked, who was
scenarios.errors_recovery: a spawn failure reports the program and directory and no task is

scenarios.title: Attach and detach repositories
scenarios.expected_result: a project holds a set of repositories, one of them primary, and the primary is derived rather than typed. What the strip says about them is current, not current-as-of-whenever-the-page-was-opened.
scenarios.errors_recovery: an unreadable folder shows in the file panel as unreadable rather than as empty. A refresh that fails leaves the last good reading with its error carried, rather than blanking the strip or raising a banner every ten seconds.

scenarios.title: Open a file and save it against an agent's edit
scenarios.expected_result: a file can be edited beside working agents without either side losing
scenarios.errors_recovery: an unreadable or oversized file reports why and the window can be

scenarios.title: Read what an agent says it is doing
scenarios.expected_result: the operator can follow progress without reading a transcript, and can never mistake what an agent asserted for what the system measured.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a claim always carries its age, so a three-hour-old account cannot sit unmarked beside a four-second-old measurement; the surface being down means sessions still run and simply cannot report.

scenarios.title: Read captured session history, including recovery after a crash
scenarios.coverage: `apps/desktop/src/main/transcriptRecovery.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/main/transcripts.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/ProjectHome.tsx`, migration 63; focused SQL/reader tests in harness packet. Native full walkthrough not yet accepted.
scenarios.expected_result: known history survives the executor and app restart, with uncertainty preserved rather than invented success.
scenarios.errors_recovery: lost reply retries the same command; mismatched receipt never deletes local evidence; current runtime generations remain owned by their pending finalizer. Background recovery never stops an agent or releases a writer lease.

scenarios.title: See who remembered something, and what memory could not answer
scenarios.expected_result: the operator can tell a fact they wrote from a fact an agent asserted, and can see whether memory is being used and whether it is answering — instead of inferring both from how full it looks.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a retrieval that cannot be recorded never fails the search it was recording — the answer matters more than the bookkeeping, and the failure is logged.

scenarios.title: Evaluate the shift from vibe coding to passion coding
scenarios.coverage: none from this repository — the subject is `passioncode-ai.github.io`, and a citation this tree cannot resolve is not a
scenarios.expected_result: the reader can explain the category transition, product/kernel boundary and present status without inferring autonomous operation or a public runtime.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a private or unavailable repository is labelled by role rather than offered as a download; no page function depends on a script or external API.

scenarios.title: See what this project remembers, and what it could not answer
scenarios.coverage: `apps/desktop/src/shared/memoryOverview.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/main/memoryOverviewRead.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/MemoryOverviewSection.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/memoryOverview.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/MemoryOverviewSection.test.tsx`, `apps/desktop/test/memory-overview-read.test.mjs`. `draft` rather than `built` because the drill-in this scenario's step 3 describes is CO-153 and unbuilt
scenarios.expected_result: the project's knowledge is inspectable — the operator can say what is stored, who put it there, whether it is being used and whether it answers.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a store that cannot be read never blanks the others; it reports its own failure in its own row. A store nobody has asked about says NOT READ, which is neither the empty answer nor the refusal; a count that came back without a number is not zero; and a reading that includes any unasked store is partial rather than whole.

scenarios.title: Rejoin a project by reading its decisions
scenarios.expected_result: the operator rejoins the work knowing why it stands where it does, without reading a transcript.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a compile that fails leaves the previous digest visible WITH its age, and says the refresh failed — never a blank band.

scenarios.title: Work a board the agents keep current
scenarios.coverage: `apps/desktop/src/shared/ladder.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/Board.tsx`, `apps/desktop/test/operating-surfaces.test.mjs`, `ProjectHome.tsx#BoardSection`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/BoardSection.test.tsx`. UX28-04 closed the rejection path and the three rules above; the keyboard move is a native `select` and stays one, which is the card's own exclusion. `draft` rather than `built` because no run has watched an agent move its own card on a live board
scenarios.expected_result: the state of the project's work is a project fact that agents maintain, with every card accountable to a person or an agent by name.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a move that fails to journal snaps back and says so — the board never shows a state the journal does not hold. A REFUSAL and a REJECTION are different events and end the same way: the card returns to where the record has it, and the reason is announced. A command that succeeded while the refetch after it did not leaves the card where the operator put it and says it is not yet confirmed by the record, with a check-again that reconciles rather than re-issuing the command.

scenarios.title: Ask the manager, and get an artefact rather than advice
scenarios.expected_result: a conversation with the manager terminates in an artefact — a binding, a proposal, a task or a journalled decision — or in nothing, stated.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a creation that fails leaves the specification on screen with the reason, so the operator can fix it rather than retype it. A send whose result is unknown is reconciled by the same operation ID and is never discarded to free space; a stale draft never overwrites newer text; an unreadable local history is reported as unreadable, not empty.

scenarios.title: Lead with the projects actually being worked
scenarios.coverage: `apps/desktop/src/shared/favourites.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/main/favourites.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/EstateHome.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/favourites.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/halfShipped.test.tsx`. `draft` rather than `built` because no run has watched an operator with more than six projects choose which to release
scenarios.expected_result: a portfolio of many does not bury the two being worked today.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a pin that fails to record leaves the row unchanged and reports it. A pin refused because the set is full is NEITHER a failure nor a success — nothing is written and nothing is dropped — and it is reported as its own thing, because a full disk and a full favourites list are not the same news.

scenarios.title: Read what the estate has actually done
scenarios.coverage: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/ProfileSection.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/types.ts#EstateSummary`, the `estate:summary` handler in `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts`. CORRECTED 2026-09-10 (UX28-03): this row cited `apps/desktop/src/shared/digest.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/DigestSection.tsx` and `apps/desktop/src/shared/digest.test.ts`, which are the project page's "where we left off" band and not the manager's profile at all — so the digest appeared covered by a scenario about something else, and had no scenario of its own until SCN-090
scenarios.expected_result: the profile is a measurement surface for the estate, checkable line by line.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a figure whose register cannot be read shows as unavailable with the reason, never as zero.

scenarios.title: Rejoin a task by reading its own page
scenarios.expected_result: the operator can rejoin any piece of work cold, and knows for every line whether a person or an agent put it there.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a resource whose target is gone says so in place and keeps the reference, rather than disappearing and taking the trail with it. **A failed save keeps the text in the box** — a save that fails and also empties the field is the same data loss the save existed to prevent. A response for a task the operator has already left is discarded, never rendered under the task now on screen. One edit blurred twice is recorded once.

scenarios.title: Judge direction from goals and the graph
scenarios.expected_result: the operator can name the next dependency before a goal closes and distinguish intended work from recorded history.
scenarios.errors_recovery: partial reads retain known goal/task membership with coverage and age; invalid normative dependency cycle is refused by the command with a named relation; historical cycles are not rejected by that rule. A closed list NOBODY COUNTED is treated as a floor, exactly as one known to be cut short is: "unknown" is not "nothing was cut", and a missing coverage is the same claim as unknown.

scenarios.title: See what a project's agents may do, and hold them to it
scenarios.coverage: `apps/desktop/src/shared/agents.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/agentSpec.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/agentSpec.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/harness.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/main/harnessRead.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/HarnessSection.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/HarnessSection.test.tsx`, `apps/desktop/test/harness-read.test.mjs`, `scripts/check-surface-tools.mjs`. `draft` rather than `built` because the skills half is M123's and unbuilt, and no run has watched an operator hold an agent to this panel
scenarios.expected_result: what agents may do in this project is visible, and the rules they follow cannot drift from the product that enforces them.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a server whose grant cannot be read shows as unavailable with the reason; the agent that depends on it does not start and says which grant it is waiting for. Every figure that comes from a read can say it could not be read, and one refusal of several is a PARTIAL reading rather than a whole one. A figure that is estate-wide says so, because a grant is not scoped to a project.

scenarios.title: Find anything the estate holds from one field
scenarios.coverage: `apps/desktop/src/shared/search.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/main/searchRead.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/SearchPanel.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/search.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/SearchPanel.test.tsx`, `apps/desktop/test/search-read.test.mjs`. `draft` rather than `built` because no run has watched a person find something they could not otherwise name
scenarios.expected_result: one door to everything, and an honest account of where the answer was looked for.
scenarios.errors_recovery: a failed store never blanks the page; it reports itself and the rest still answers. A refused store is never listed among the places searched, and "nothing matches" cannot be claimed while one is silent.

scenarios.title: Watch every agent from one screen
scenarios.coverage: `apps/desktop/src/shared/agents.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/HarnessSection.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/agents.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/keyedRead.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/EstateAgents.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/EstateAgents.reads.test.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/TerminalView.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/sessionOrder.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/shared/sessionOrder.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/EstateAgents.terminal.test.tsx`. UX28-02 keyed the two readings and rendered each one's failure; UX28-13 attached the console, ordered the list and added the task route as a third keyed read. UX28-14 gave the screen a THREE-track grid (`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/styles.css`, `.project-columns-3`): it had been using the two-track `.project-columns` with three children, so the session list took the wide track, the console took the narrow one and the third panel wrapped to a second row — and `col-main`/`col-side` have no rule anywhere, so placement was positional all along. STILL NOT covered: the staleness AGE this scenario's `stale` state names is computed by `keyedRead.ts#staleness` and not shown here; the per-agent END action named in UI elements, which is destructive and has no confirmation idiom on this screen; and the launch control at the head of the list, which SCR-39's Elements names and nothing builds.
scenarios.expected_result: the operator moves between agents without opening a project per agent, and can tell in seconds which one needs them.
scenarios.errors_recovery: an agent whose console cannot attach says so and keeps the rest of the screen usable. The history and the repository reading fail SEPARATELY: one refusing names itself in its own panel and leaves the other's answer on screen, and a failed reading drops its payload rather than leaving the previous answer standing as current.

scenarios.title: Answer a scoped question and see whether work received it
scenarios.expected_result: The answer is durable and the operator can distinguish decision commit from receipt by the working agent.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Timeout after commit retries the same command ID; a competing answer returns the current receipt; delivery retry never records a second answer or grant. A queued receipt is not proof of delivery: a current fenced owner may finish; an expired pre-write claim may be reclaimed; a possible prior write stays outcome_unknown and is not replayed. Stop or manual terminal input invalidates pending readiness; source failure is not an empty Board.

scenarios.title: Inspect a manager settlement and override it by a new decision
scenarios.expected_result: The operator can inspect and correct accountable decisions without a fabricated explanation of model reasoning.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A stale decision or trust revision is revalidated on commit; a rejected override retains input and explains recovery; past effects require their own compensating work.

scenarios.title: Read one execution iteration without confusing report and observation

scenarios.errors_recovery: A missing agent's projects show the gap as attention, not as a failure of Fabric.

scenarios.title: See MCP servers through Project Observatory
scenarios.expected_result: MCP servers are seen apart from agents, from one inventory.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A server that does not answer is shown as such, never removed from the list.

scenarios.title: MCP servers without Project Observatory
scenarios.expected_result: The operator always knows how complete the list is.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A read failure names Observatory's answer; Fabric never scans configs itself as a hidden second inventory.

scenarios.title: Give Fabric a task; it picks the project and the agent
scenarios.expected_result: Any task goes through one conversation, and the work is receipted in its project.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A plan Fabric cannot make (no capable agent) says so and offers to make an agent (SCN-121).

scenarios.title: First use of an agent in a project
scenarios.expected_result: An agent enters a project only through admission and binding, in one confirmation.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Registry unavailable is distinct from admission failed (SCN-004 rule). Nothing with an effect runs before binding.

scenarios.title: An agent waits for my choice
scenarios.expected_result: No job stalls silently and none proceeds on a guess.
scenarios.errors_recovery: An expired point names what happened to the job (cancelled by the agent or still waiting); a secret is never asked in the form — it goes to the credential flow.

scenarios.title: A job fails or its result is unknown
scenarios.expected_result: Failures are named and recoverable; unknown outcomes are resolved, not duplicated.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Retry reuses the idempotency key where the capability requires it.

scenarios.title: A coding agent calls Fabric within its grant
scenarios.expected_result: One protocol connects agents, and every call is scoped and traced.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A credential never appears in a URL, argument or log line.

scenarios.title: Ask the floating Fabric to change what is on screen
scenarios.expected_result: Edits are sentences to Fabric, grounded in what the operator is looking at.
scenarios.errors_recovery: An ambiguous target ("this" with two selections) makes Fabric ask which; context is knowledge, never authority.

scenarios.title: Micro-controls on the screen
scenarios.expected_result: Tiny edits need no conversation; everything larger does.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A micro-change that breaks a check (for example moving an effect before its checker) is refused with the check's reason.

scenarios.title: Fabric composes a pipeline and I approve it
scenarios.expected_result: Repeated work runs as a proven, versioned pipeline.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A proposal that cannot pass the checks is never saved.

scenarios.title: A pipeline fails its checks
scenarios.expected_result: Broken pipelines are stopped at design time with an exact reason.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Checks are structural; the mandatory checker remains the guard for meaning.

scenarios.title: Reuse a global pipeline; replace an agent
scenarios.expected_result: Pipelines survive agent changes and travel between projects.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Missing bindings block the run before it starts, with the stage named.

scenarios.title: Read a run as one graph
scenarios.expected_result: A chain of agents reads as one workflow.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A node whose payload is private shows that it exists, not its content.

scenarios.title: Debug a failed branch; an incomplete trace
scenarios.expected_result: Failures are found in the graph; gaps in evidence are visible.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Missing trace data never fabricates nodes.

scenarios.title: Use Fabric tools in a project and globally
scenarios.expected_result: Scripts that replace agent work are first-class and traced.
scenarios.errors_recovery: An empty Tools section explains that tools come from accepted optimizer proposals or from asking Fabric.

scenarios.title: A tool cannot be enabled or fails
scenarios.expected_result: Only tested scripts run; failures are ordinary, visible failures.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A tool runs inside the caller's execution context; it never gets wider access than the caller.

scenarios.title: Accept an optimizer proposal
scenarios.expected_result: Token-saving changes are grounded in real runs and applied only by the operator.
scenarios.errors_recovery: The proposal cannot accept itself (DEC-0012).

scenarios.title: Decline or wait on a proposal
scenarios.expected_result: The optimizer learns from refusals and never pushes thin evidence.
scenarios.errors_recovery: none.

scenarios.title: Ask Fabric to make a new agent
scenarios.expected_result: Agents are made inside Fabric and come out protocol-correct and wired in.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Any failed stage keeps the draft (SCN-123).

scenarios.title: Turn an existing project into an agent
scenarios.expected_result: Existing work becomes a Fabric agent without hand-wiring.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Files are proposed on a branch in the project's repository; nothing is written to its main line.

scenarios.title: Agent production fails a gate
scenarios.expected_result: No half-made agent is admitted; nothing is lost.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A gate failure never removes an earlier admitted revision.

scenarios.title: Fabric answers from memory with sources
scenarios.expected_result: Fabric does not make the operator repeat themselves, and shows what it relied on.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Search covers Russian and English text in full.

scenarios.title: Nothing in memory, or memory unavailable
scenarios.expected_result: Fabric never invents a memory.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Unavailable memory never degrades into an unsourced answer.

scenarios.title: First run: name, look, coding agents, where to start
scenarios.expected_result: The first run is finished once; `settings.firstRun.completedAt` holds the moment; the operator is on the chosen path or home.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A look that is not saved says why and offers Continue without saving. A detection that fails says so and offers Check again. An installation already holding projects is never walked back through the first run; an unknown project list never triggers it.

scenarios.title: Add an existing project from one folder
scenarios.expected_result: One new Project holding exactly the chosen folder; nothing in the folder changed.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A failed create says why, keeps the folder and the name; a retry is the same create (the same id), never a second Project. A folder outside the window's grant is refused by the main process.

scenarios.title: Scan a projects folder and tick what becomes a Project
scenarios.expected_result: One Project per ticked repository; nothing created for an unticked one; the last scan is kept so unticked candidates can be imported later.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A walk stopped by its bound says the list is not the whole folder. A row that failed to import is marked "not added", stays ticked, and Add retries it with the same id. A scan error says why and offers to choose again.

scenarios.title: Create a new project in a new folder or as an idea
scenarios.expected_result: A new Project; with a folder, the folder exists under the chosen parent and, when asked, is a git repository on `main`.
scenarios.errors_recovery: A folder that already exists, an invalid folder name, a location outside the window's grant and a failed mkdir/git init each say what happened; the Project is not created. A failure after the folder was made reuses that folder on retry.

scenarios.title: Start a new agent inside a project
scenarios.expected_result: The operator is at the project's agent form; the agent is created there (SCN-121).
scenarios.errors_recovery: An unknown project list shows loading, never "no project".

scenarios.title: Convert an agent built elsewhere into a Fabric agent
scenarios.expected_result: A Fabric-compatible agent in the registry, with the probe's receipt; or a red receipt and no registry entry.
scenarios.errors_recovery: Not applicable while planned; the screen never offers an action that pretends to run.

flows.goal: what agents may do in a project is visible, and the contract they follow is the tool list rather than a document
flows.entry_points: the harness panel on the project page; the manager chat
flows.success_exit: an agent is bound with its mandatory skill and either runs or names the grant it is waiting for
flows.mermaid_source:
flowchart TD
  A[Screen: SCR-31 Project page] -->|harness| B[Screen: SCR-35 Project harness]
  B -->|add an agent| C{Specification confirmed?}
  C -->|no| B
  C -->|yes| D[binding.hired journalled with the mandatory skill]
  D --> E{Grant present?}
  E -->|no| F[Agent not running - the grant is named]
  F -->|issue grant| E
  E -->|yes| A
  B -->|open a tool| T[Screen: SCR-38 Harness tool]
  T -->|back| B

flows.title: Answer and continue accountable work
flows.goal: Resolve an authored question while distinguishing commit from delivery.

 D -->|decision evidence| E[Screen: SCR-33 Decision history]

 D -->|open addressed work| T
 T -->|back to question| D

flows.title: Inspect storage import declared data and restore an archive
flows.goal: Keep declared mirror import distinct from restoring an archive into a fresh Estate ([ADR-0079](../adr/0079-private-conversation-archives-preserve-history-not-authority.md)).
flows.entry_points: Memory sync, estate storage settings, import or restore action.
flows.success_exit: Import receipt, or a restored Estate that is opened after an explicit choice and restart.

flowchart TD
 M[Screen: SCR-34 Project memory] -->|storage sync| S[Screen: SCR-47 Storage and sync]

review_choices.title: Первый результат до полной настройки организации
review_choices.choice: Проект и задача доступны без обязательной команды, интеграций и manager setup. Запуск отдельно требует допустимого execution context.
review_choices.tradeoff: Пользователь раньше фиксирует полезную работу; интерфейс обязан показывать незавершённый setup и точную причину блокировки запуска.

review_choices.title: Четыре адресуемых графа
review_choices.choice: История агента, история проекта, целевой план и решения открываются отдельно. Превью остаются на страницах проекта и агента.
review_choices.tradeoff: Чуть больше маршрутов, зато стрелки не меняют смысл при переключении фильтра. Везде есть список и путь назад.

review_choices.title: Основные действия на виду; детали раскрываются
review_choices.choice: На главной — нужные решения и проекты; настройки, доказательства и редкие controls раскрываются по месту.
review_choices.tradeoff: Редактор персонального набора controls остаётся будущей задачей M187, а не дополнительным конструктором сейчас.

review_choices.title: Встроенный и внешний manager проходят общий lifecycle
review_choices.choice: Одна роль, сменяемый binding, измеренные capabilities, один effective writer epoch и явная передача контекста.
review_choices.tradeoff: Не обещаем native session resume там, где admission его не подтвердил. ADR0046 остаётся proposed.

review_choices.title: Локальный сбор и исходящий feedback разделены
review_choices.choice: Предложение ADR0047: local intake включён и отключаем; outbound отдельно выключен до проверенной активации.
review_choices.tradeoff: Ваш прежний вариант default-on outbound сохранён как альтернатива. «Удалили user ID» недостаточно для обещания анонимности.

review_choices.title: Default для новых запусков; текущий разговор переключается отдельно
review_choices.choice: Сохраняем conversation и Task, создаём новый Session/TaskRun; при неподтверждённом resume не обещаем продолжение.

review_choices.title: Автосмена доступна после явного включения
review_choices.choice: Разрешённый pool, стратегия и enrollment позволяют менять аккаунт без повторного confirmation; общий coordinator подтверждает сохранность разговора.
review_choices.tradeoff: Без сертифицированного resume и свежей identity/quota режим остаётся недоступным; автоматический выбор не отменяет границы исполнения.

options.tradeoff: Полный authority review полезен при включении организации, но откладывает первую работу и требует решений до знания проекта.

options.shape: Project draft в tab→первая Task→контекстно необходимый root/readiness→первый результат; организационные настройки позже.
options.tradeoff: Требует явных readiness и незавершённого setup состояний, зато сохраняет progressive adoption.

flow_alternatives.reason: Соответствует vision principle 5 и S09. Аккаунты/роль/рутину показывать в момент, когда они нужны выбранному действию; не выдавать zero-repo HOME за доступный workspace.
